1. Load the borough crime-rate table and the adjacency (“neighbours”) list into pandas DataFrames / dicts.

2. Detect missing values in the crime-rate column.  
   • Drop any borough whose own crime-rate is NaN; it will not be examined or reported.  
   • When a remaining borough’s neighbourhood set contains a dropped borough, simply omit that neighbour from all calculations (i.e. sum only the available numeric values).  
   • After the drop, record len(remaining_boroughs) as data_points_used.

3. For every remaining borough i:  
   a. Build the local area Ωᵢ = {i } ∪ {all available neighbours of i}.  
   b. Compute local_sumᵢ = Σ (crime-rate) over Ωᵢ.

4. Across all remaining boroughs, compute  
   • μ = mean(local_sum)  
   • σ = sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of local_sum.

5. Obtain a standard z-score for each borough: zᵢ = (local_sumᵢ – μ) / σ.

6. Determine significance:  
   • |zᵢ| > 2.576  ⇒ 99 % confidence hot/cold spot.  
   • |zᵢ| > 1.960  ⇒ 95 % confidence hot/cold spot.  
   • zᵢ > 0 ⇒ HOT;   zᵢ < 0 ⇒ COLD.

7. Assemble a results list of every borough whose zᵢ is significant, formatted “BoroughName (HOT, z-score = <value>)” or “… (COLD, z-score = <value>)”, rounded to three decimals.

8. Print:  
   • data_points_used = <integer>  
   • FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}    (or “FINAL ANSWER: none” if results is empty).

This plan uses only pandas/numpy, treats missing values by exclusion, and evaluates whether the combined borough-plus-neighbours crime total is unusually high or low city-wide.

coder_result.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# 1. Load data
crime_path = 'chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_second_half_2017.csv'
adj_path   = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

crime_df = pd.read_csv(crime_path)
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(adj_path)

# 2. Drop boroughs whose own crime value is missing
crime_df_clean = crime_df.dropna(subset=['crime_rate_value']).copy()
available_boroughs = set(crime_df_clean['borough'])

# 3. Build a neighbour dictionary, omitting any neighbours that were dropped
neigh_dict = {b: set() for b in available_boroughs}
for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    if b in available_boroughs and n in available_boroughs:
        neigh_dict[b].add(n)

# 4. Compute local sums: borough + all its available neighbours
crime_series = crime_df_clean.set_index('borough')['crime_rate_value']
local_sums = {}
for b in available_boroughs:
    local_area = {b} | neigh_dict[b]          # union of itself and neighbours
    local_sums[b] = crime_series.loc[list(local_area)].sum()

local_sum_values = np.array(list(local_sums.values()))

# 5. City-wide statistics for local sums
mu  = local_sum_values.mean()
sig = local_sum_values.std(ddof=1)            # sample std-dev

# 6. z-scores
z_scores = {b: (s - mu) / sig for b, s in local_sums.items()}

# 7. Significance test
results = []
for b, z in z_scores.items():
    if abs(z) > 2.576:                # 99% confidence
        label = 'HOT' if z > 0 else 'COLD'
        results.append(f"{b} ({label}, z-score = {z:.3f})")
    elif abs(z) > 1.960:              # 95% confidence
        label = 'HOT' if z > 0 else 'COLD'
        results.append(f"{b} ({label}, z-score = {z:.3f})")

# 8. Print outputs
data_points_used = len(available_boroughs)
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")

if results:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
